video_title: How Warriors’ Al Horford would have fared in NCAA’s NIL era #DubsTalk #NBCSportsBayArea #basketball

quotes.summary_phrase: Al Horford on the challenges of NIL for young college athletes
quotes.excerpt: I hope that they're getting some sort of guidance

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified reporter
text_blocks.text: NIL, what are your thoughts about NIL and just how it's affected college and everything, just these kids? And also what would have been like back then maybe for you too with a little NIL?

text_blocks.speaker: Al Horford
text_blocks.text: I worry a little bit about the kids. I do want them to get paid and rewarded, but I hope that they're getting some sort of guidance because I've talked to some of the younger guys who are coming up and I'm asking questions and things like that. It's great that they're getting rewarded, they rightfully should, but then it's like we have to find a way to help them to put them in a better position so they can be successful with the money that they're making.

quotes.social_post: Al Horford says he worries about young college athletes handling NIL money without proper guidance. He supports them getting paid but emphasizes the need for mentorship to help them manage their finances successfully.

structured.context: Al Horford discusses his thoughts on the impact of NIL on young college athletes and the need for financial guidance.

quotes.speaker: Al Horford
quotes.summary_phrase: Al Horford reflects on his own maturity during his college career
quotes.excerpt: I don't think I had the maturity level like that to handle that
quotes.quote: If I had NIL back then, I don't know if it would have been good for me. When you're 18, 19, all of a sudden you get all this money, it's so tempting to go buy a nice fancy car. For me, it was actually a good thing because I was driven to lock in and just get to the league, but I don't think I had the maturity level like that to handle that. So I would say that I'm okay with it, but I like NIL, but I just think that we need to find a way to help them so they can be better with their money.
quotes.social_post: Al Horford admits he is not sure he would have handled NIL money well at 18 or 19 years old. He says he lacked the maturity at the time and might have been tempted to buy a fancy car instead of focusing on his goal of reaching the NBA.

structured.context: Al Horford reflects on whether he would have been mature enough to handle NIL money during his own college career.
